Creating impact

How HBCU ECP scholars are using DEEDS to solve real problems for real clients in Southeast Queens and beyond.

9th Grade · Physics · Protest Safety Devices

Scholars investigated the physics of crowd dynamics and force to understand why large-scale protests can turn dangerous, then designed, built and drop-tested wearable safety devices to reduce impact, using real force and time-of-impact data to redesign and refine their prototypes.

Deliverable · Engineering memo to the NYCLU

9th Grade · Social Studies / Leadership Studios · Claiming Our Voices

Scholars researched the historical and present-day fight for voting rights and how elections actually work in NYC, then designed a Youth Voter Guide zine to help first-time voters from the African diaspora register, research candidates, and show up with power.

Partners · NYC Votes · The Andrew Goodman Foundation · League of Women Voters NYC

9th Grade · AI & Media · Community App Design

Scholars used Figma to design community-focused apps addressing real local problems, including a concept connecting people experiencing homelessness with donated food, clothing and shelter resources, then presented their research and design rationale to a public audience.

100%

Pass rate across all Early College courses in Year 1, HBCU ECP's founding year.

Key features of the HBCU ECP model

HBCU culture, early college and real-world learning, held together by personal and identity development.

1

HBCU Culture & Identity

The House System, HBCU Fridays, Mentorship Mondays and Wellness Wednesdays build belonging and college identity, rooted in P.O.W.E.R. values.

2

Early College

Dual enrollment with Delaware State University lets scholars earn a high school diploma alongside college credit, with automatic admission to DSU at graduation.

3

DEEDS

Discover, Examine, Engineer, Do/Deploy, Share/Sustain: a standards-aligned project-based learning cycle where every module tackles a real community challenge.

4

Real-World Learning

Success coaching, campus visits, internships and local partnerships stack into an ecosystem, including 54 work-based learning hours built into the program.

Culture is infrastructure

Daily rituals like Morning Call & Response, House Huddles, homecoming, Marching Band and Step team sit alongside rigorous early college coursework, not as enrichment tacked onto the day, but as part of the same coherent scholar experience.

Why this matters now

Three things are changing at once. HBCU ECP already has an answer to each.

Dual enrollment is where the credit is going

Schools will increasingly need to count early college coursework and work-based learning toward graduation. HBCU ECP scholars are already earning college credit and work-based hours in Year 1.

AI means scholars need judgment, not just answers

DEEDS gives scholars a real client and no answer key: a NYCHA resident, a first-time voter, a landlord who won't fix the problem. Nothing a chatbot can finish alone was worth assigning.

Black and Brown scholars deserve to see the dream before they arrive on campus

HBCU culture isn't an add-on at HBCU ECP. It's built into every House, every Friday, every advisory period, starting in 9th grade.

Partner with us

Transcend partners with HBCU Early College Prep to build and coach this model, in partnership with Delaware State University, UNCF and XQ Institute. Here is what that support looks like.

Sharpen your vision

You know what you want for your scholars. We help you say it precisely enough to build from, with your staff and partners in the room.

What it looked like at HBCU ECPFounding vision and mission built with school leadership, grounded in HBCU culture, dual enrollment and real-world learning.

Build the curriculum + programming

We support you in designing or refining the modules your scholars' DEEDS experience runs on, aligned to your standards and your vision.

What it looked like at HBCU ECPDEEDS module design and revision for Government/Economics and Physics, College Composition and AP Human Geography module design, and the Leadership Studios scope and sequence.

Coach your educators

New practices need support, not a binder. We coach the DEEDS cycle itself, using a non-evaluative coaching frame so teachers can adjust mid-project.

What it looked like at HBCU ECPNon-evaluative DEEDS coaching for founding teachers, plus summer PD design spanning curriculum mapping, assessment scheduling and instructional vision work.
